elements.element: No minimum purchase commitment imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer commits to purchase no minimum amount of Services"

elements.element: Fees payable only for usage or ordered Services

elements.evidence: "in each of the next three years" retained; no 12-month limitation
"with reduction or termination rights." — no 30-day notice mechanic

reasons: The preferred level is fully achieved: no minimum amount, take-or-pay deleted, and payment only for Services ordered or used.

Minimality fails on the affirmative grant "with reduction or termination rights": once there is no minimum commitment, no reduction or termination right is needed to reach the preferred position, and the phrase creates an unqualified, mechanic-less right (no notice period, no procedure) grafted onto a commitment sentence.

Residual wording ("commits to purchase no minimum amount ... in each of the next three years") is internally awkward; a cleaner minimal edit would strike the commitment sentence or replace it with a short "Customer has no minimum purchase commitment; Fees are payable only for Services ordered or used."
Fallback elements (12-month scope, 30 days' notice, true-up) are absent, but that is immaterial because the locked preferred level is satisfied and the levels are not to be combined.
Clause 2.2 (order of precedence) is untouched and remains effective; no unrelated commercial term is disturbed.
